replaceSection._why: CDC p367: complete glossary list (their note stops at Integration; P-S kept from the book)
items: **Algorithm:** A set of step-by-step instructions followed to solve a problem or perform a task.
**Alignment:** The arrangement of text, images or objects in a straight or organised position.
**Application:** A computer program designed to perform a particular task.
**Application Programming Interface (API):** A set of rules that allows different software applications to communicate and share information.
**Array:** A data structure used to store several values under one name.
**Artificial Intelligence (AI):** Technology that enables computers and machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.
**Authentication:** The process of checking the identity of a user before allowing access to a system.
**Automation:** The use of technology to perform tasks with little or no human involvement.
**Augmented Reality (AR):** Technology that adds computer-generated information or objects to a real-world environment.
**Backup:** A copy of data kept separately so that it can be restored if the original data is lost or damaged.
**Boolean Expression:** A logical expression that produces either a TRUE or FALSE result.
**Boolean Logic:** A system of logic that uses TRUE and FALSE values to make decisions.
**Brochure:** A printed or digital publication used to provide information about a product, service or organisation.
**Bug:** An error or fault in a computer program that causes it to produce incorrect results or behave unexpectedly.
**Circuit:** A complete path through which electric current flows from a power source through connected components.
**Cloud Computing:** The delivery of computing services such as storage, software and processing over the internet.
**Cloud Storage:** A service that allows users to store and access data over the internet.
**Coding:** The process of writing instructions in a programming language to make a computer perform tasks.
**Combinational Circuit:** A digital circuit whose output depends only on its current inputs.
**Computer Network:** A group of connected computers and other devices that communicate and share resources.
**Conditional Statement:** A programming instruction that allows a program to make decisions based on specified conditions.
**Cybersecurity:** The practice of protecting computers, networks, applications and data from digital attacks and unauthorised access.
**Cyber Threat:** A possible danger that can damage, disrupt or gain unauthorised access to computer systems or data.
**Database:** An organised collection of related data stored for easy access, management and updating.
**Database Management System (DBMS):** Software used to create, store, organise, retrieve and manage data in a database.
**Data Privacy:** The protection of personal information from unauthorised access, use or disclosure.
**Data Protection:** Measures taken to safeguard data against loss, damage, theft or unauthorised access.
**Data Security:** The protection of information against unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure or destruction.
**Debugging:** The process of identifying and correcting errors in a computer program.
**Desktop Publishing (DTP):** The use of computer software to design and produce publications such as posters, brochures, newsletters and books.
**Digital Circuit:** An electronic circuit that processes information using binary values (0 and 1).
**Digital Circuit Simulator:** Software that allows users to design and test electronic circuits on a computer without physically building them.
**Digital Footprint:** The record of information a person leaves behind when using the internet and digital services.
**Electronic System:** A combination of electronic components that work together to perform specific functions.
**Encryption:** The process of converting readable information into an unreadable form to prevent unauthorised access.
**Event:** An action or occurrence, such as clicking a button, that can trigger a response in a computer program.
**Expression:** A combination of values, variables and operators that produces a result.
**Firewall:** A security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic to prevent unauthorised access.
**Flowchart:** A diagram that uses symbols and arrows to represent the steps involved in solving a problem or carrying out a process.
**Function:** A reusable block of code designed to perform a particular task in a program.
**Graphical User Interface (GUI):** A way of interacting with a computer using visual elements such as icons, menus, buttons and windows.
**Hardware:** The physical parts of a computer or electronic device that can be seen and touched.
**Hyperlink:** A clickable text, image or button that connects users to another webpage, document or section of a presentation.
**Hypertext Mark-up Language (HTML):** A language used to structure and organise content on web pages.
**Image Placement:** The positioning of pictures or graphics in a document or publication to improve its appearance and communication.
**Integration:** Connecting different programs, databases, or devices so they can share and use data together. Learning integration helps systems work smoothly as a single unit.
**Power Supply System:** The parts of a robot that provide electricity so it can work properly. Learning to set up a power supply ensures devices run safely and reliably.
**Real-Time Monitoring:** Seeing data instantly as it is collected from sensors or devices. It helps you make quick and accurate decisions based on live information.
**Remote Monitoring:** Checking and controlling robots or systems from far away using the internet or networks. It allows you to manage devices without being physically present.
**Robotic Structure:** The main body or frame of a robot that holds all the parts together. Designing a good robotic structure helps the robot move and function efficiently.
**Sequential Circuit:** A circuit that can remember past inputs as well as the current input. It is useful for tasks that require memory, like counters or timers.
